neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert but severely disinhibited throughout the exam. Makes inappropriate sexual comments to the female medical assistant. Laughs inappropriately when discussing his job loss. MMSE 21/30 — loses 3 points on delayed recall (0/3), 3 points on serial sevens, 2 points on orientation to date and month. Cannot copy interlocking pentagons (perseverates on strokes). Clock drawing severely abnormal: numbers placed randomly outside clock face. FAB 10/18 — fails go/no-go, environmental autonomy, conflicting instructions, and lexical fluency. Category fluency (animals): 7 in 60 seconds (severely impaired). Cannot explain proverbs (concrete interpretation). Utilization behavior: automatically picks up pen on desk and begins writing without instruction.
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: Intact. Pupils equal and reactive. Extraocular movements full. Mild bilateral facial hypomimia noted.
neurological_exam.motor: Normal bulk. Mild bilateral upper extremity rigidity (cogwheel quality) without tremor. Strength 5/5 throughout.
neurological_exam.sensory: Intact to light touch and pinprick bilaterally.
neurological_exam.reflexes: 2+ bilaterally. Bilateral grasp reflex present. Snout and palmomental reflexes present bilaterally (frontal release signs).
neurological_exam.gait: Mildly shuffling, reduced arm swing. No apraxia.
neurological_exam.additional: Hyperorality observed during exam — patient took crackers from desk without being offered. Poor hygiene noted by examiner: food stains on clothing, body odor.

patient.chief_complaint: Two-year progressive personality change with disinhibition, compulsive eating, loss of empathy, and poor hygiene.
patient.history_present_illness:
Mr. K. is a 58-year-old right-handed White male brought in by his wife of 30 years for progressive personality and behavioral changes over the past 2 years. His wife reports that the change began subtly — he became less interested in conversation, more irritable, and started making inappropriate comments at family gatherings. Over the following year, the changes became unmistakable: he began making sexually explicit remarks to female neighbors, laughed at his granddaughter's injury, and showed complete indifference when their dog died. She describes him as having 'lost his soul.' He has developed compulsive behaviors: he insists on eating the same three meals daily, paces the living room for exactly 30 minutes every evening, and has begun hoarding items from grocery stores. His diet has changed dramatically — he craves sweets and high-calorie foods and has gained 18 pounds. His personal hygiene is severely degraded; his wife must physically guide him to shower.

Professionally, he retired from accounting 2 years ago after colleagues reported he was making errors in client accounts and had made inappropriate comments to staff. He shows no insight into his deficits and is not distressed. His wife has discovered he has been making online purchases totaling over $14,000, mostly buying things that he immediately forgets having ordered. His alcohol use has escalated from 1-2 beers occasionally to 6-8 beers nightly, which he denies entirely. He has never had psychiatric illness and there is no family history of dementia. Neurological review of systems is otherwise negative.

signal_characteristics.T1: knife-blade gyral atrophy on coronal sequences

additional_observations: Ventricles mildly enlarged commensurate with frontal atrophy
mri.impression: Severe bilateral frontal and anterior temporal lobe atrophy with knife-blade gyral pattern and mild caudate atrophy. Normal hippocampal volume. Posterior parietal and occipital cortex preserved. Clinical correlation recommended.

findings.finding: Severe hypometabolism, symmetric, involving prefrontal, orbitofrontal, and cingulate cortex

advanced_imaging.impression: Severe bilateral frontotemporal hypometabolism — a pattern consistent with a frontotemporal metabolic profile. Posterior cingulate cortex metabolism preserved. Clinical correlation recommended.

findings.finding: No significant amyloid uptake; SUVR below positivity threshold

output.impression: Negative — sparse-to-no amyloid neuritic plaque density. Global SUVR 0.94, below positivity threshold. Clinical correlation recommended.

output.interpretation: Opening pressure: 125 mmH2O. WBC: 2 cells/mm3 (N/A PMN/N/A lymph). Protein: 44 mg/dL. Glucose: 61 mg/dL (ratio 0.69). Abeta42: 798 pg/mL (normal). Total tau: 231 pg/mL (normal). Phospho-tau 181: 38 pg/mL (normal). NfL: 2,104 pg/mL (elevated — consistent with neurodegeneration). 14-3-3 protein: negative.

findings.result: Severely impaired — Trails B: >3 minutes with multiple errors; WCST perseverative errors 85th percentile; Stroop: 1st percentile; FAB 10/18
Severely impaired — Faux Pas Test: 3/20; complete failure on perspective-taking and social inference tasks
Moderately impaired but predominantly retrieval-based (frontal) — free recall impaired, cued recall relatively better; CVLT-II: 15th percentile with cueing benefit
Intact naming; reduced verbal fluency consistent with frontal dysfunction
FrSBe: severe disinhibition (98th percentile), severe apathy (91st percentile), executive dysfunction (96th percentile); NPI-Q caregiver distress: 24/36

output.impression: Neuropsychological profile consistent with probable behavioral-variant frontotemporal dementia. Severely impaired executive function (Trails B, Stroop 1st percentile, WCST perseverations 85th percentile) and social cognition (Faux Pas 3/20) with retrieval-predominant memory pattern and intact confrontation naming. Clinical correlation recommended.

findings.finding: Minimal non-specific signal — no tau accumulation above threshold

output.impression: No Alzheimer-typical tau distribution identified. Temporal meta-ROI SUVR 1.10, below tau-positivity threshold. Clinical correlation recommended.

output.proposed: Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (sertraline 100 mg/day) for behavioral symptoms in bvFTD
interactions: Metformin + sertraline: minimal interaction; monitor blood glucose as SSRIs can affect glycemic control
contraindications: Acetylcholinesterase inhibitors (donepezil, rivastigmine, galantamine): no established benefit in frontotemporal dementia; may exacerbate behavioral disinhibition
warnings: Metformin + sertraline: SSRIs may affect glycemic control; monitor blood glucose
Benzodiazepines: increased fall risk and potential paradoxical disinhibition in elderly patients
Antipsychotics: increased cerebrovascular event risk in dementia; use with caution and specialist oversight
alternatives: Trazodone: sedating antidepressant; used off-label for agitation and sleep disturbance
Fluvoxamine: SSRI; off-label use for compulsive behaviors

background.sleep_features: normal vertex waves and sleep spindles

general.summary: No directly applicable, high-quality evidence was retrieved for this query. Recommend correlating with current society guidelines.

differential.key_features: Amyloid PET negative, CSF Abeta42 normal, frontal-predominant pattern with posterior sparing on MRI and FDG-PET
Age of onset 58, progressive neurodegeneration on imaging, severe neuropsychological deficits
No urinary incontinence, no gait apraxia, atrophic pattern on MRI rather than hydrocephalus
2-year course too slow for CJD, no myoclonus, no DWI restriction, 14-3-3 negative

Severe bifrontal hypometabolism, posterior cortex spared

Refer to social work for caregiver support and safety planning
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Financial and driving safety concerns addressed

critical_actions: Diagnose bvFTD based on clinical criteria (Rascovsky 2011): progressive behavioral syndrome with disinhibition, apathy, compulsive behaviors, hyperorality, executive dysfunction, and frontal atrophy/hypometabolism
Assess driving safety and financial decision-making capacity — patient has already caused significant financial harm
Consider SSRI (sertraline, fluvoxamine) for compulsive behaviors and disinhibition
Provide caregiver education and refer to FTD Association
contraindicated_actions: Acetylcholinesterase inhibitors (no benefit; may worsen agitation)
Memantine (limited/no evidence in bvFTD; may worsen behavioral symptoms)
High-dose benzodiazepines (worsen disinhibition and increase fall risk)
Reassurance that changes are due to alcohol — escalating alcohol use is a symptom of frontal disinhibition in FTD, not the cause
key_reasoning_points: Classic bvFTD triad: disinhibition + compulsive behaviors + loss of empathy with frontal-predominant atrophy and hypometabolism
The combination of knife-blade frontal atrophy on MRI and severe frontal hypometabolism on FDG-PET is highly characteristic of FTD
Preserved episodic memory (better with cues) and absence of posterior cortex involvement distinguishes bvFTD from Alzheimer disease
Alcoholic beverages escalation is a symptom of frontal disinhibition in FTD — not the cause of cognitive decline
Financial and driving safety must be addressed urgently in bvFTD due to impaired judgment and impulsivity
